Since the \(H^{p+q}(X,-)\) commute with filtered inductive limits, it follows from (8.7.6.2) that this morphism of spectral sequences is an isomorphism at the level of the \(E_2^{p,q}\). Consequently it induces an isomorphism on the abutments, whence (8.7.7.1). For every \(A\)-Module \(N\), one has a spectral sequence (V 5.3). \[ E_2^{p,q} = H^p(X,R^q \mu_{i*}(N)) \Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(\mu_i^*(X),N) . \] The commutation with filtered inductive limits of the functors \(H^n(\mu_i^*(X),-)\) then follows from the analogous properties of the functors \(H^n(X,-)\) and \(R^n \mu_{i*}\) (8.7.6).

When the topoi \(F_j\), \(j \in \mathrm{ob}(I)\) are coherent and when the transition morphisms are coherent, the hypothesis made on \(X\) (resp. \(F_i\)) in 8.6.7 is satisfied when \(X\) (resp. \(F_i\)) is coherent (5.2). One knows moreover that in this case \(\mu_i^*(X)\) (resp. \(\underline{F}\)) is coherent (8.3.13).

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 8.7.9

Let \(i\) be an object \(I\), \(M_i\) a left \(A_i\)-Module, \(L_i\) a right \(A_i\)-Module possessing a resolution of the type: \[ P_{i,k} \to P_{i,k-1} \to \dots \to P_{i,0} \to L_i \to 0 \] where, for every integer \(k\), \(P_{i,k}\) is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of objects of the form \(A_i|X\) (IV 11.3.3), where \(X\) satisfies the hypotheses of 8.7.7. If, besides the hypotheses of 8.7.1, the fibred topos \(F\) is right-flat (8.6), one has canonical isomorphisms, for \(n \leq k-1\): \[ \text{(8.7.9.1)} \qquad \operatorname{Ext}^n_{\underline{A}}(\underline{F}; \mu_i^*(L_i), \mu_i^*(M_i)) \simeq \varinjlim_{f:j\to i} \operatorname{Ext}^n_{A_j}(F_j; f^*(L_i),f^*(M_i)) . \]

Denote by \(P_{i,\bullet}\) the resolution of \(L_i\). Since \(F\) is right-flat, for every \(f : j \to i\), \(f^*(P_{i,\bullet})\) is a resolution of \(f^*(L_i)\) and \(\mu_i^*(P_{i,\bullet})\) is a resolution of \(\mu_i^*(L_i)\) (8.6). These resolutions allow one to construct two spectral sequences which converge respectively to the two members of (8.7.9.1), and a morphism between these two spectral sequences. At the level of the \(E_1^{p,q}\) this morphism is an isomorphism (8.7.7.1). It therefore induces an isomorphism on the abutments.

footnotes.html: (1) To fix ideas we shall take left modules.

pages.title: 9. Appendix. Criterion for the existence of pointsby P. DELIGNE

blocks.html: 9. Appendix. Criterion for the existence of pointsby P. DELIGNE

blocks.title: Proposition
blocks.html:
Proposition 9.0

Every locally coherent topos \(S\) has enough points.

The question being local on \(S\), one may suppose the topos \(S\) defined by a site \(\mathcal{S}\), in which finite projective limits are representable and such that every covering \(f_i : U_i \to U\) admits a finite subcovering. It suffices to prove that if \(f : \mathscr{F} \to \mathscr{G}\) is not a monomorphism, then there exists a point \(x\) of \(\mathcal{S}\) such that \(f_x\) is not injective. By hypothesis, there exist \(U \in\) ob \(\mathcal{S}\) and \(a, a' \in \mathscr{F}(U)\) such that \(a \neq a'\) and \(f(a) = f(a')\). Replacing \(\mathcal{S}\) by \(\mathcal{S}/U\), one reduces to the

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 9.1

If \(a\) and \(a'\) are two distinct global sections of a sheaf \(\mathscr{F}\) on a site \(\mathcal{S}\) satisfying the preceding hypotheses, then there exists a point \(x\) of \(\mathcal{S}\) such that \(a_x \neq a'_x\).

Let \(P = (U_i)_{i \in I}\) be a projective system in \(\mathcal{S}\), indexed by a filtered ordered set \(I\). For every sheaf \(\mathscr{H}\) on \(\mathcal{S}\), one sets \(P(\mathscr{H}) = \varinjlim \mathscr{H}(U_i)\), and, for every \(V \in \mathrm{Ob}\, \mathcal{S}\), one sets \(P(V) = \varprojlim \mathrm{Hom}(U_i,V)\). The functors \(P(\mathscr{H})\) and \(P(V)\) commute with fibre products. If the functor \(P(V)\) transforms coverings into surjective families of functions, it is a morphism of sites from the punctual topos into \(\mathcal{S}\), and \(P(\mathscr{H})\) is the corresponding fibre functor.

If \(P = (U_i)_{i \in I}\) and \(Q = (V_j)_{j \in J}\) are two projective systems in \(\mathcal{S}\), one says that \(Q\) refines \(P\) if \(I\) is a subset of \(J\) endowed with the induced order and if \(P\) is the restriction of \(Q\) to \(J\). One then has morphisms of functors from \(P(\mathscr{H})\) into \(Q(\mathscr{H})\) and from \(P(V)\) into \(Q(V)\).

Whatever \(P\) may be as above, we shall denote by \(a_p\) and \(a'_p\) the images in \(P(\mathscr{F})\) of \(a\) and \(a'\). Lemma 9.1 follows from the following lemma, in which one takes for \(P\) the projective system indexed by \(\{0\}\) and reduced to the final object of \(\mathcal{S}\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 9.2

Whatever \(P\) may be as above satisfying \(a_p \neq a'_p\), there exists \(Q\) refining \(P\), satisfying \(a_Q \neq a'_Q\), and such that, whatever the covering \(f_i : V_i \to V\) and \(f \in Q(V)\) may be, \(f\) is in the image of one of the \(Q(V_i)\).
We shall first prove:

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 9.3

Let \(P = (U_i)_{i \in I}\) satisfy the hypotheses of lemma 9.2, \(f_i : V_i \to V\) a finite covering in \(\mathcal{S}\), and \(f \in P(V)\). There exists \(Q\) refining \(P\), satisfying \(a_Q \neq a'_Q\) and such that the image of \(f\) in \(Q(V)\) is in the image of one of the \((V_i)\).

There exist \(i_0 \in I\) and \(f' \in \mathrm{Hom}(U_{i_0},V)\) which define \(f\). For \(i \geq i_0\), set \(U_{i,k} = U_i \times_V V_k\), this fibre product being defined by \(f'\). One knows that \((V_k)\) is a covering of \(V\), hence \(U_{i,k}\) is a covering of \(U_i\); the following arrow will be injective (for \(i > i_0\)): \[ \mathscr{F}(U_i) \to \prod_k \mathscr{F}(U_{i,k}) \] Passing to the limit, taking into account that finite products commute with filtered inductive limits, one sees that \[ P(\mathscr{F}) \to \prod_k \varinjlim \mathscr{F}(U_{i,k}) \] is injective, hence that there exists \(k\) such that \(a_p\) and \(a'_p\) have distinct images in \(\varinjlim_{i>i_0} \mathscr{F}(U_{i,k})\). Let then \(I_0 = \{i \mid i \geq i_0 \text{ and } i \in I\}\), and \(J = I \amalg I_0\). One orders \(J\) by saying that \(j' \leq j''\) if the images of \(j'\) and \(j''\) in \(I\) satisfy \(j' \leq j''\) and if one does not have \(j' \in I_0\), \(j'' \in I\). The \(U_i\) and \(U_{i,k}\) are indexed by \(J\), and form a refinement \(Q\) of \(P\), such that \(a_Q \neq a'_Q\), and such that the image of \(f\) in \(Q(V)\) is in the image of \(Q(V_k)\).

blocks.title: Lemma
blocks.html:
Lemma 9.4

Let \(P = (U_i)_{i \in I}\) satisfy the hypotheses of lemma 9.2. There exists \(Q\) refining \(P\), such that \(a_Q \neq a'_Q\), and such that for every finite covering \((V_k)\) of an open \(V\) of \(S\), and every \(f \in P(V)\), the image of \(f\) in \(Q(V)\) is in the image of one of the \(Q(V_k)\).

Let \(E\) be the set of triples formed of an open \(V\) of \(S\), a finite covering \((V_k)\) of \(V\) and \(f \in P(V)\). Let \(\leq\) be a well-ordering on \(E\) and \(\overline{E}\) the set deduced from \(E\) by adjunction of a largest element, denoted \(\infty\). We shall define by transfinite recursion on \(e \in \overline{E}\) refinements \(Q_e\) of \(P\), satisfying \(a_{Q_e} \neq a'_{Q_e}\) and such that
(i) if \(e' \leq e\), then \(Q_e\) refines \(Q_{e'}\).
(ii) if \(e = (V,(V_k),f)\), then the image of \(f\) in \(Q_e(V)\) is found in the image of one of the \(Q_e(V_k)\).

Suppose the \(Q_e\) already defined for \(e' < e\). If \(e\) is the first element of \(E\), set \(Q'_e = P\). If \(e\) has a predecessor \(e-1\), set \(Q'_e = Q_{e-1}\). Otherwise, let \(Q'_e\) be the projective system with index set \(\bigcup_{e'<e} I_{e'}\), which refines the \(Q_{e'}\), for \(e' < e\). In this case, one has \[ Q'_e(\mathscr{F}) = \varinjlim_{e'<e} Q_{e'}(\mathscr{F}) \] so that, in all cases, \(Q'_e\) refines the \(Q_{e'}\), for \(e' < e\) and satisfies \(a_{Q'_e} \neq a'_{Q'_e}\).
One obtains the required projective system \(Q_e\) by applying lemma 9.3 to \(Q'_e\), and to \(e = (V,(V_k),f)\) (resp. by taking \(Q_e = Q'_e\) if \(e = \infty\)).
The projective system \(Q_\infty\) satisfies lemma 9.4.
Lemma 9.4 allows one to define, by recursion on \(n\), a sequence \(Q_n = (U_i)_{i \in I_n}\) of projective systems in \(\mathcal{S}\) such that
(ii) \(Q_{n+1}\) refines \(Q_n\)
(iii) \(a_{Q_n} \neq a'_{Q_n}\)
(iv) Whatever the covering \(f_k : V_k \to V\) and \(f \in Q_n(V)\) may be, the image of \(f\) in \(Q_{n+1}(V)\) is found in the image of one of the \(Q_{n+1}(V_k)\).
The projective system \(Q\), with index set the union of the \(I_n\), which extends the various \(Q_n\), then satisfies lemma 9.2. The proof shows moreover that:

blocks.title: Corollary
blocks.html:
Corollary 9.5

Let \(\mathcal{S}\) be a site, in which the fibre products are representable and such that every covering in \(\mathcal{S}\) admits a finite subcovering. Let \(c\) be the cardinal \(\sup(\aleph_0, \operatorname{card}(\mathrm{Fl}\,\mathcal{S}))\). Then there exists a very dense set of points of \(\mathcal{S}\), such that

  1. (i)

    \(\operatorname{card}(X) \leq 2^c\)

  2. (ii)

    if \(x \in X\) and \(U \in \mathrm{Ob}\, \mathcal{S}\), then \(\operatorname{card}(U_x) \leq c\).
